answer: Requiring a slashable stake per identity stops Sybil attacks because each new account must lock real capital before it can vote or claim rewards. Catching one fake agent destroys its stake, so forging N identities costs N times the bond rather than a few cents of compute. Here each vine must be rooted in collateral before it yields, and the whole orchard of linked wallets is forfeited when collusion is found. Rewards are also split across all claimants, so the spiral of clones shrinks each attacker's payoff while its cost keeps rising. Honest single identities stay cheaper.
